source.title: Deep Grokking: Would Deep Neural Networks Generalize Better?
source.authors: Si-Min Fan; Razvan Pascanu; Martin Jaggi

page_placements.theme: Representation geometry and cross-model alignment vary around interpolation

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: It reports test-accuracy trajectories over training for deep MLPs, a different setting and measure from the original double-descent studies. The reported trajectories bear on epoch-wise double descent, but do not test the model-size or sample-size error curves.
record.gate_note: The paper measures test accuracy over training steps and reports delayed or multi-stage generalization, so these trajectories bear on V2. Its depth and training-set-size comparisons do not report a test-error sweep with a peak near interpolation, and the training-set-size results do not establish that more data raises test error near that threshold. Feature-rank double descent is a different measure from test error and is recorded under fits_no_version. Linear-probe accuracy and weight-norm observations are not rows for the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is a grokking study. MLPs on MNIST use large initialization and small weight decay, chosen to produce delayed generalization. It reports test-accuracy curves only as figures. The text never describes test error rising and falling again over training. Footnote 1 distinguishes its rank double descent from double descent on loss curves. Double descent appears only as related work 'could be connected'. Its results do not bear on whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that deep MLPs are more prone to grokking and show multi-stage generalization. They also conclude that feature-rank descent tracks generalization transitions better than weight norm. They explicitly distinguish their rank double descent from double descent on loss curves.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines delayed and multi-stage generalization in fixed-width ReLU MLPs on MNIST using large initialization and small weight decay; it does not reproduce the original double-descent size, epoch, or sample-size error sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported generalization trajectory varies with MLP depth, training-set size, and weight decay.

fits_no_version.finding: In deep MLPs (8- and 12-layer) on 7000 MNIST points, and in some weight-decay settings, two-stage test-accuracy surges coincide with a double descent of layer feature ranks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-stage generalization in deep networks aligns with a double-descent pattern in internal feature rank.

record.problems: The relevant trajectories are shown only in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The experiments use MLPs on MNIST, and the authors leave experiments on other architectures to future work.
record.rows_left_out: No additional test-accuracy trajectory rows were left out. Linear-probe accuracy and weight-norm measurements were excluded because they are not the test-error behavior named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: No sweep of model size or width. Depth is varied only for grokking onset.
Only grokking-induced trajectories are reported. No fall-rise-fall in test error is described or quantified.
Sample size is varied (2000/5000/7000), but there is no interpolation-threshold test-error analysis.
Not addressed. Feature rank is offered as an indicator of grokking, not of double-descent peak location.
Weight decay is varied for grokking, not for double-descent peaks. Label noise is not studied.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges V2' label is withdrawn. Grokking is a separate phenomenon induced here on purpose via large initialization. The figures give no readable values, and the text's silence about a test-error rise is not evidence that V2 fails.

versions.untested_parts: No test-error curve across model sizes is reported, and no peak near the size that just fits the training set is identified.
The paper studies training trajectories for MLPs on MNIST, not other model classes or datasets; it reports test accuracy rather than directly tabulated test error.
Although training-set sizes are varied, the paper does not test whether increasing sample size near an interpolation threshold raises test error.
No double-descent risk curves across model classes are tested.

Feature-rank changes are associated with generalization transitions, but the paper does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
Weight decay is varied, but label noise or variance as a driver, double-descent peaks splitting, and disappearance under optimally tuned regularization are not tested.
The paper does not re-count model complexity using an effective parameter measure or test whether that transforms a second descent into a U-shaped curve.

tranche.reason: The experiments study grokking and feature-rank trajectories, a different construct from the risk or test-error double descent in the claim versions. They neither test nor use those claims.
